explanation: A judge and leader of Israel who fought against the Ammonites and won, but had to fulfill a tragic vow to sacrifice his own daughter.
A people who lived east of the Jordan River and were enemies of the Israelites. Jephthah led the Israelites in battle against them.

A solemn commitment or declaration that one will do something specific. Jephthah made a vow to God to sacrifice the first thing he met after his victory over the Ammonites, which turned out to be his daughter.
One of the twelve tribes of Israel who came into conflict with Jephthah and the Gileadites. This resulted in a civil war between the two groups.
A region east of the Jordan River where Jephthah and his people, the Gileadites, lived. They fought against the Ephraimites in an internal struggle.

A word used as a test to distinguish Gileadites from Ephraimites during the conflict. The Ephraimites had trouble pronouncing "s," so those who could not say "shibboleth" correctly were identified as Ephraimites and killed.
